title: Latency and Throttle Incident Primer
content:
Purpose:
This primer is a compact runbook for the most common API degradations we see in production: persistent timeouts, elevated 429 (rate-limit) errors, degraded or chunked streaming, and sudden increases in internal error rates. It's intended for first responders (oncall SREs) who need fast triage steps and short-term mitigations. Longer-term remediation belongs in a post-incident RCA owned by the responsible service team.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted API frontends, dedicated pools, and private deployments that use Redwood's serving runtime.
- Assumes responder has access to Redwood Console, Grafana dashboards (latency/error/429), Kibana/ES logs, and Kubernetes/host-level access for Dedicated/Private.
- For privacy-regulated customers, use the private console and audit logs as applicable.

High-level signals (what to look for first):
1) Latency spike: P95/P99 token generation latency rising above SLO band for > 3 minutes.
2) Increased client timeouts: Surge in 408/499 client-side timeouts or retry storms.
3) 429 spike: sustained 429 rate > baseline by 5x or absolute 429% > 2% of requests for 5+ minutes.
4) Streaming degradation: truncated streams, missing chunks, or long gaps between partial events.
5) Internal error rate: 5xx increase in model-backend or gateway logs (500/502/503/504) beyond baseline.

Quick triage (first 10 minutes):
A. Establish incident channel: #sre-incident-[short-id] on Slack, declare scope and severity, add service owners. Use template (see below).
B. Snapshot dashboards: capture last 30m and 6h graphs for throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, 429 rate, inflight requests, queue depth, and CPU/GPU utilization.
C. Killblame checklist (fast heuristics):
   - Is traffic pattern different? (deploys, campaigns, new release) -> check recent deploys (GitHub PRs, rollout window).
   - Is model variant change or fallback in effect? (model routing logs) -> check rollout flags, model pins.
   - Is the issue global or region-specific? -> compare region dashboards.
D. Check autoscaler and capacity: are new pods being created? any crashloops? (kubectl get pods, describe, check autoscaler logs).
E. Tail logs for errors and backpressure signs: gateway logs for 429 producers (rate limiter hits), runtime logs for OOM/quantization failures, model host logs for mangled responses.

Commands and metrics to run immediately:
- kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
- kubectl -n inference describe hpa/<service> or check autoscaler events
- curl -s "<console-metrics-endpoint>?query=requests_per_second{service=~\".*gateway.*\"}"
- grep -i "rate limit" /var/log/gateway/* || use console traces to find rate-limiter keys
- Check queue depth: metric 'inference_request_queue_depth' per host/pool
- Model host health: check GPU metrics (GPU util, mem), NVMe iowait, and worker thread stalls

Common root causes and quick mitigations:
1) Retry storms and client side retries -> Mitigation: temporarily enable stricter ingress throttles and add short lived 429 backpressure headers (Retry-After) and a server-side suppression mechanism for aggressive clients. Coordinate with API-gateway team to apply temp rules.
2) Sudden traffic spike (legit) -> Mitigation: scale up dedicated pool (if capacity available) or enable burst capacity for Hosted tier. If scaling slow, enable rate limiting with graceful degradation: reduce max tokens, disable streaming for heavy routes, or return cached responses for repeated prompt fingerprints.
3) Model slowdowns (KV cache churn, cold-starts) -> Mitigation: pin stable model variants, fall back to cheaper/older model under a compatibility matrix, reduce batch sizes to bring latency down. Consider toggling 'inflight-limiter' config to cap per-model concurrency.
4) Resource exhaustion (OOMs, GPU saturation, disk IO) -> Mitigation: offload to spare pool, drain unhealthy nodes, restart affected pods, and reply with degraded placeholder if required.
5) Streaming-specific failures (chunking/gaps) -> Mitigation: switch to non-streaming endpoint for new requests, enable smaller flush intervals, toggle 'stream-fallback' bridge that emits partial cached summary rather than streaming raw tokens.

Escalation and when to page:
- Page oncall engineer for model-serving and gateway if: 5xx rate > 3% or 429 rate > 10% of traffic for 10+ minutes, or if latency is blocking business-critical routes (billing, auth).
- Page backend infra if host-level metrics show sustained >90% GPU or CPU for >5 minutes or persistent OOMs.
- Page product/CS if a paying customer is impacted and SLA windows may be missed.

Short-term patch examples (fast actions):
- Toggle rollout to previous model version: update route pin in routing table -> rollback.
- Apply routing rule to divert 10% traffic to fallback pool (canary) to stabilize latency.
- Temporarily set max_tokens cap on heavy endpoints to 512.
- Turn off long-poll streaming for certain endpoints via feature flags.
- Apply emergency autoscaler manual scale: kubectl scale --replicas=<n> deployment/<pool-deployment>

Operator's checklist (box-tick form):
[ ] Create incident channel and note start time
[ ] Snapshot dashboards (attach images)
[ ] Identify earliest error signal and correlate with deploys/rollouts
[ ] Collect logs from gateway, runtime, model hosts for t-15m..now
[ ] Apply a short mitigation (throttle/rollback/scale/drain) and note action and timestamp
[ ] Monitor effect for 10 minutes; if not improving, escalate

Communication templates (Slack):
- Incident Kicker (first message):
  • Incident: API latency/429 spike affecting /v1/generate and streaming routes
  • Severity: P2 (if >1 customer affected) or P1 (if >1 hour or SLAs in danger)
  • Owner: @maya (SRE), Requested: model-serving and api-gateway oncall
  • Quick notes: snapshot attached, initial hypothesis = traffic spike causing queueing.

- Customer-facing blurb (short):
  We’re experiencing elevated latencies and rate-limit responses on text-generation APIs. Engineers have applied temporary mitigations and are actively working on stabilization. We’ll provide an update in 30 minutes.

Post-incident actions (first 72 hours):
1) Capture complete timeline with action timestamps and metric sweeps.
2) Assign RCA owner and classify root cause (traffic, resource, software, config).
3) If degraded streaming was involved: run regression tests for streaming flush intervals and re-check default buffer sizes.
4) Update routing and fallback matrices to make future automatic failovers less disruptive.
5) Add or refine synthetic monitors: add a streaming-endpoint heartbeat that verifies chunk cadence under load.

Longer-term mitigations and experiments to consider:
- Per-customer token budgeting with early-exit heuristics to avoid single-tenant storms.
- Adaptive batching that monitors per-model latency tails and reduces batch size when P95/P99 increase.
- Circuit-breaker with staged degradation: streaming -> non-streaming -> cached summary -> 429.
- Backpressure-aware SDK guidance for customers (client side jitter, exponential backoff, and honoring Retry-After).
- Improve observability: tag traces with model-variant, batch-size, and kernel path.

RCA checklist prompts (for post-incident):
- Which component introduced the dominant latency (gateway, runtime, model host)?
- Were there any recent config/rollout changes? (feature flags, model pins)
- Did autoscaler behave within thresholds? Was scale-up delayed?
- Were any clients responsible for disproportionate traffic?
- Did caches (KV/prefix) experience thrash and evictions?
- Were there disk/GPU IO anomalies?

Notes-to-self / open questions (work items):
- Run a chaos experiment that simulates steady-state 2x traffic with 10% tail to measure autoscaler responsiveness.
- Investigate tighter default Retry-After semantics for streamed partial responses.
- Write a small diagnostic endpoint that returns per-request batch-id and model-variant to make tracing simpler.

Appendix: Useful dashboard queries and metric names
- inference.requests.total, inference.errors.5xx, inference.rate_limited.429, inference.latency.p95, inference.latency.p99
- gpu.utilization{host}, host.iowait, process.oomevents, inference.request_queue_depth
- trace tag: model_variant, batch_size, kernel_path

End of primer.
